item.title: 1941: DiMaggio Named AL MVP Over Ted Williams, 56-Game Streak
item.description: Joe DiMaggio of the New York Yankees is named 1941's American League MVP over Ted Williams of the Boston Red Sox (15 of 24 first-place votes and 291 points for DiMaggio, 8/24 and 254 for Williams). DiMaggio, who established his 56-game hitting streak as an MLB record between mid-May and mid-July, batted .357 with 30 home runs and led the AL in RBI (125), while Williams closed the season with a MLB-leading .406… Photo: Tom Sande (Public domain).

item.title: 2024: McCullough Named Manager of Miami Marlins
item.description: On November 11, 2024, McCullough was named the manager of the Miami Marlins.

item.title: 2022: Badgers Host Basketball Doubleheader in Brew City Battle
item.description: On November 11, 2022, the University of Wisconsin Badgers hosted a basketball doubleheader at American Family Field called the "Brew City Battle". Photo: Carol H. Highsmith (Public domain).

item.title: 2022: Free Agents May Sign With Clubs Other Than Former Teams
item.description: First Day of free agents may sign contracts with a club other than a former club

item.title: 2021: Art Stewart, 94, Royals Front Office Executive and Scout
item.description: Art Stewart, 94, front office executive and director of scouting for the Kansas City Royals from 1969 to 2021 who started his scouting career in 1953 with the New York Yankees.

item.title: 2021: Harper Wins Second Sliver Slugger, Ohtani Earns First
item.description: The 2021 Sliver Slugger Awards were announced winners included Bryce Harper from the Philadelphia Phillies who won his second sliver slugger award and Shohei Ohtani from the LA Angels wins his first career sliver slugger award. Photo: All-Pro Reels from District of Columbia, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2020: Bieber and Bauer Win AL and NL Cy Young Awards
item.description: Shane Bieber of the Cleveland Indians and Trevor Bauer of the Cincinnati Reds Respectively win the AL And NL CY Young Awards. Photo: Erik Drost (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2019: Ragsdale Promoted to Major League Field Coordinator
item.description: Ragsdale was promoted to the major league staff, as major league field coordinator, on November 11, 2019. Photo: Adam Moss from East Amherst, New York, United States (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2015: Posey Named Wilson Defensive Player of the Year
item.description: On November 11, 2015, Posey was named winner of the 2015 Wilson Defensive Player of the Year award, given to the best defensive catcher in MLB. Photo: SD Dirk (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2014: Tigers-Giants Join MLB All-Stars in 80th Anniversary Game
item.description: The series also celebrated the 80th anniversary of the establishment of Japan's professional baseball by holding an exhibition game of a joint team of Hanshin Tigers and Yomiuri Giants against the MLB All-Stars at the Koshien Stadium on November 11, 2014.

item.title: 2014: Abreu and deGrom Win Rookie of the Year in AL and NL
item.description: José Abreu of the Chicago White Sox and Jacob deGrom of the New York Mets earn the Rookie of the Year Award in the American League and National League, respectively. Photo: EricEnfermero (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2011: Florida Marlins Officially Renamed Miami Marlins
item.description: At 9:00 pm, the Florida Marlins are officially renamed the Miami Marlins. They move to Marlins Park the next year.

item.title: 2009: Tacoma Considers $30 Million Renovation of Cheney Stadium
item.description: On November 11, 2009, it was announced the City of Tacoma was considering a $30 million renovation to Cheney Stadium. Photo: Ken Lund (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2001: McGwire Announces Retirement With 583 Career Home Runs
item.description: Mark McGwire announces his retirement. His 583 career home runs place him fifth on the all-time list. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2001: Tadashi Sugiura, 66, Hall of Fame NPB Pitcher and Manager
item.description: Tadashi Sugiura, 66, Hall of Fame NPB pitcher and manager who played for the Nankai Hawks from 1958 to 1970 and managed them from 1986 to 1989.

item.title: 1998: Dierker Named NL Manager of the Year After 102-Win Season
item.description: Larry Dierker, who led the Houston Astros to a team record 102 wins and a playoff appearance was named National League Manager of the Year. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1986: Mike Scott Edges Valenzuela to Win NL Cy Young Award
item.description: The Astros' Mike Scott (98 points, 15 first-place votes) nips Fernando Valenzuela (88, nine) to win the 1986 NL Cy Young Award. Scott led his circuit in bWAR (8.2), earned run average (2.22), innings pitched (275<small>1/3</small>), and strikeouts (306). Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1981: Valenzuela Wins NL Cy Young, First Rookie to Do So
item.description: Fernando Valenzuela of the Los Angeles Dodgers wins the National League Cy Young Award, becoming the first rookie to win the award. Photo: Jim Accordino (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1978: Bennie Borgmann, 80, Longtime Cardinals Scout
item.description: Bennie Borgmann, 80, minor-league infielder and manager and NBA basketball player who served the St. Louis Cardinals as a longtime scout; member of Basketball Hall of Fame

item.title: 1977: Rangers Sign Free-Agent Pitcher Doc Medich From Mets
item.description: The Rangers sign free-agent pitcher Doc Medich, most recently with the New York Mets.

item.title: 1962: Ken Hubbs Becomes First Rookie to Win Gold Glove Award
item.description: Ken Hubbs of the Chicago Cubs becomes the first rookie to win a Gold Glove Award.

item.title: 1943: BBWAA Bestows Its 1943 MLB Most Valuable Player Awards
item.description: The Baseball Writers' Association of America bestows its 1943 MLB Most Valuable Player Awards.

item.title: 1940: Dodgers Acquire Kirby Higbe From Phillies for $100,000
item.description: Brooklyn Dodgers general manager Larry MacPhail acquires starting pitcher Kirby Higbe from the Philadelphia Phillies in exchange for pitchers Bill Crouch and Vito Tamulis, catcher Mickey Livingston and $100,000. Higbe won 14 games this past season for the financially struggling Phillies; in 1941, his 22 victories as a Dodger will lead National League pitchers. Photo: Unknown (Public domain).
